recentItems.title: Walking the Long March: An American's journey
recentItems.description:
The Long March remains a powerful chapter in China's history, 90 years after the victory of the Chinese Red Army in 1936. What can a journey along the Long March route reveal about its history and spirit? How can shared experiences help young people from different countries better understand one another? In this special episode of The Hub, Wang Guan speaks with Zhavier Harris, marketing and communications manager at the Springfield Urban League, who followed in the footsteps of the Long March. Together, they explore his journey through places connected to the Long March, and examine the connections he discovered between people and communities.

recentItems.title: From a Moche headdress to Chancay Port: 55 years of China and Peru
recentItems.description:
A golden Moche headdress – one of Peru's most important national treasures. In 1988, a tomb in northern Peru was looted, and the artifact disappeared. Nearly 20 years later, it finally made its way home. After its return, it was rarely put on public display in Peru. Today, it's part of the "Maize, Gold and Jaguar" exhibition at Beijing's Capital Museum, thousands of kilometers from where it was made. As China and Peru mark 55 years of diplomatic ties, behind the exchange of treasures lies something larger: an enduring friendship, and a partnership built on shared prosperity.

recentItems.title: China's five initiatives and the future of BRICS
recentItems.description:
At the BRICS Summit in New Delhi, Chinese President Xi Jinping called on the group to be a pioneer in innovation, peace and stability, exchanges among civilizations and global governance reform. He also followed that with five initiatives for greater BRICS cooperation, covering AI and trade and development, the digital economy, smart manufacturing and talent development. 
How should we all understand China's vision for the future of BRICS? Can the group help transform the Global South from rule-takers to rule-shapers? As BRICS enters its third decade, can it turn an ambitious agenda into concrete results? 

Guests in this episode of Dialogue are Yin Zhiguang, professor of International Politics at Fudan University, Radhika Desai, director of the Geopolitical Economy Research Group, and Vinicius G. Rodrigues Vieira, associate professor of Economics and International Relations from the Armando Alvares Penteado Foundation.

recentItems.title: Three takeaways from the EU's State of the Union
recentItems.description:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has delivered her annual State of the European Union address in Strasbourg.
Here are three key points: 
1. The risks of AI – Von der Leyen warned that AI development could move beyond human control. She called for a slower, safer approach, though she offered few concrete proposals for regulation. 
2. Social media and children – She proposed banning social media for under-13s, with stricter supervision for teenagers up to 15. Some groups support the idea but argue that authorities should focus on addictive algorithms rather than broad age-based bans.
3. Closer ties with Canada – Von der Leyen proposed opening a path for Canada to become the EU’s first associate member. It comes as Ottawa's ties with Washington worsen.

recentItems.title: Has AI surpassed human intelligence?
recentItems.description:
The people building it are starting to walk away. In recent weeks, researchers at OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind have quit to warn the public that AI could escape human control, with one putting the odds of it killing us all within a decade at over 10%. In the latest episode of "Season of AI & Basic Sciences," CGTN's Tian Wei sits down with Paddy Cosgrave – founder and CEO of Web Summit, one of the world's biggest tech conferences – to ask who's actually leading, why innovation looks so different in China and the West, and whether anyone can govern this thing. Take a listen.

recentItems.title: AmCham China president: Why are US companies still staying in China?
recentItems.description:
What continues to keep US companies in China amid changing global supply chains? Michael Hart, president of the American Chamber of Commerce in China, points to China’s market, advanced manufacturing and engineering capabilities. He says these factors will continue to shape US-China business ties in the decades ahead.
